keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Freising row). The page gives no area. Five soft circles: Freising 11.75E 48.40N 14 km (the page names the Isar-river towns of the Yserrain without a place); Werdenfels 11.10E 47.49N 14 km ('the acquisition of the rich county of Werdenfels in the late 13th century'); Innichen 12.28E 46.735N 7 km (acquired 783); Bischoflack 14.31E 46.165N 14 km (donated 973); Wolzer and Katschtal 14.2E 47.15N 12 km (given in 1007). Cadore is a county in the Patria del Friuli on the page, with no year, and is left out.

ledger.note: 1294: the prince-bishopric. 'In 1294, the bishop was raised to the status of prince-bishop' and became 'an Estate of the Empire enjoying imperial immediacy' (lead: 'from 1294 until its secularisation'). The abbey dates from circa 723-730 and the diocese from 739; the earlier acquisitions (Innichen 783, Burgrain 808, Bischoflack 973, Wolz and Katsch 1007) came before the state starts and are drawn inside the 1294 keyframe.
November 1802: the enclaves. 'In November 1802, Bavarian officials and troops entered the city'; the Styrian and Slovenian enclaves 'were annexed by Austria'.

region.text: the Styrian and Slovenian enclaves (Bischoflack, Wolz and Katsch)

ledger.note: November 1802: secularisation. 'In November 1802, Bavarian officials and troops entered the city'; 'the territory of the prince-bishopric was annexed to Bavaria' (infobox 'Mediatised to Bavaria and Austria: 1802'; 'secularised in the course of the mass secularisations of 1802-03').

certainty.note: The page gives no area; the five circles are stand-ins for the places it names.

sources.title: Prince-Bishopric of Freising
sources.note: Prince-bishop 1294; diocese 739; Innichen 783; Burgrain 808; Bischoflack 973; Wolz and Katsch 1007; Werdenfels late 13th century; Swedes 1632 and 1646; secularised 1802.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Freising row.

SCOPE. The state starts at 1294, the year the page makes the bishop a prince and an imperial estate; the earlier acquisitions are drawn inside the first keyframe. The Thirty Years' War is named ('it paid the ransom demanded by the Swedish King Gustavus Adolphus in 1632', Swedes again in 1646); the page names no battle or treaty, so no war entry and no occupation event is written. The 1821 absorption of the diocese into the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising is after the state.

SHAPES. Circles: Freising 11.75E 48.40N 14 km; Werdenfels 11.10E 47.49N 14 km; Innichen 12.28E 46.735N 7 km; Bischoflack 14.31E 46.165N 14 km; Wolz and Katsch 14.2E 47.15N 12 km. Burgrain (808) and the Yserrain towns are named without a place and are not drawn. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Freising', 'Garmisch-Partenkirchen' (Werdenfels), 'Innichen', 'Skofja Loka' (Bischoflack), 'Oberwolz'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Yserrain sale: 'Duke Ludwig of Bavaria sold several towns along the Isar River to the bishop', a few years after 1294, no year; (2) Werdenfels is 'late 13th century' with no year, so it sits inside the 1294 keyframe; (3) who took Innichen and Cadore in 1802 is not on the page; (4) no area.
